say.text: Exam-trap drill: the stems PYQs actually ask, one after another.
Where the old key and the current source disagree, you will get both.
Stem 1. Which of these is a component of classic TOF?
The four: a large VSD, an overriding aorta, RVOT obstruction and right ventricular hypertrophy. Which option is on that list?
Yes. Classic TOF is a **large, anteriorly malaligned VSD**, an **overriding aorta**, **infundibular RVOT obstruction** and **right ventricular hypertrophy**.
PYQs have keyed PDA, ASD and LVH as 'not part of TOF', and current StatPearls agrees with the four above.
ASD is tempting: it sits with TOF in the old pentalogy name and may accompany it.
But the four components listed by StatPearls and CDC include no ASD, PDA or LVH. PYQs key ASD as 'not part of TOF'.

sure_note.text: You were sure, so lock this in: ASD may accompany TOF but is not one of the four.

say.text: LVH is tempting because 'ventricular hypertrophy' is in the list. The side is the trap.
The hypertrophy in TOF is **right** ventricular. PYQs key LVH as 'not part of TOF'.

sure_note.text: You were sure, so check the side again: the fourth component is right ventricular hypertrophy.

say.text: Stem 2. Which one is part of TOF?
Right. RVH is the fourth component, and it is what upturns the apex on a chest film.
PDA is tempting because it is a very common companion in congenital heart disease. It is not one of the four.
ASD and PDA may accompany TOF, but they are not components. PYQs key PDA as 'not part of TOF'.

sure_note.text: You were sure, so remember: accompany is not the same as component.

say.text: LVH again: the same side trap. The hypertrophied ventricle in TOF is the right one.
PYQs key LVH as 'not part of TOF'.

sure_note.text: You were sure, so slow down on laterality: right, not left.

say.text: Stem 3. Pentalogy of Fallot is TOF plus what?
Yes: **pentalogy of Fallot** = TOF plus an **atrial septal defect**. PYQs expect this, CDC confirms it, and the term is old and seldom used now.
PDA is tempting as the 'fifth' lesion because it is a familiar companion. But pentalogy means TOF plus an **atrial septal defect**.

sure_note.text: You were sure, so pair it now: pentalogy goes with ASD.

say.text: A right aortic arch is a real TOF association, which makes it tempting. It is seen in 20 to 25% of TOF but it is not the fifth lesion.
Pentalogy of Fallot = TOF plus an **atrial septal defect**.

sure_note.text: You were sure, so separate association from definition: pentalogy is TOF plus ASD.

say.text: Stem 4. A chest film shows a boot-shaped heart. What produces the boot?
Yes. The classic boot has an upturned apex due to right ventricular hypertrophy.
'Big heart' is tempting because hypertrophy sounds like enlargement. But the boot is a shape, not a size: an **upturned apex** due to RV hypertrophy.

sure_note.text: You were sure, so read the sign as shape: upturned apex from RVH.

say.text: Stem 5. Which investigation is the gold standard for diagnosing TOF?
Yes. The **echocardiogram** is the gold standard and the primary diagnostic modality. The chest film only 'may classically show' the boot.

choices.label: Go deeper: the boot in the PYQ key

say.text: The boot is the famous sign, so it is tempting. But the chest film 'may classically show' it; it is not the confirming test.
The gold standard is the **echocardiogram**.

sure_note.text: You were sure, so separate 'classic sign' from 'gold standard': echo.

say.text: RV hypertrophy on ECG fits one component, which is tempting. But no tracing confirms the whole anatomy.
The gold standard is the **echocardiogram**.

sure_note.text: You were sure, so remember: signs suggest, echo confirms.

say.text: PYQs have keyed the boot-shaped heart to TOF; Radiopaedia says most infants with TOF may not show this finding.
So: key it to TOF in the exam, but do not expect every infant film to show it.
Stem 6. 'Most common cyanotic CHD beyond the neonatal period.' What is the safest approach?

choices.label: Write TOF; know it mostly presents as a cyanotic neonate
Write TOF and ignore neonatal presentation
Distrust the key and skip the question

say.text: Yes. PYQs have expected TOF as the most common cyanotic CHD beyond the neonatal period; current StatPearls says TOF most commonly presents as a cyanotic neonate.
Both fit TOF, so the exam answer stays TOF.
The answer is right, but you drop half the picture. Current StatPearls says TOF most commonly presents as a cyanotic neonate.
PYQs expected the 'beyond the neonatal period' version.
Skipping is tempting when key and source clash, but the key still points to TOF here.
Teach both: the exam wants TOF, and the current source adds the neonatal presentation.
Stem 7. A right aortic arch is seen in roughly what share of TOF?
Yes: a **right aortic arch** is seen in 20 to 25% of TOF.
'Almost all' is tempting because it is a classic association. It is a minority: 20 to 25%.
'Rare' is tempting for an anatomical variant. It is more common than that: 20 to 25%.
Sources differ on incidence: 5 to 7 per 10,000 live births in StatPearls, 3 to 5 in Garagiola and Thorne, about 3 to 6 in Gagliardi et al.
They also differ on 22q11.2 deletion: up to 15% of TOF cases versus 6% in one cohort.
Trap list: ASD, PDA and LVH are not components. Pentalogy is TOF plus ASD. Boot is a shape, echo is the gold standard.
